notes.text: Samuel Honzek is on injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Matt Coronato has taken his spot beside Mikael Backlund and Joel Farabee. That line has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 41:43 together.

Joel Hanley has not dressed for the last 11 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Jake Middleton has taken his spot beside Zayne Parekh. That pair has had 46% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 67:41 together.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 10 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.

COL.head: A big edge for the Avalanche
COL.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Calgary is on the second night of a back-to-back. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with keeping dangerous shots away.

CGY.head: The Avalanche should be favored
CGY.body: Colorado has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage, while Calgary is on the second night of a back-to-back. To pull this off, the Flames can start with keeping dangerous shots away, plus a goalie who steals the show.

story.head: Fresh legs vs. Tired ones
paras: The Avalanche won the teams’ first meeting this season, 7-3 in Calgary on Oct 8. The Flames (6-7-0) beat Seattle 6-2 last night, and the Avalanche (7-5-1) beat New Jersey 5-2 on Wednesday. Going in, the Flames are fifth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Avalanche third in the Central (tied for 16th).

The Avalanche (1st) and the Flames (2nd) both play fast, open games. The Flames have struggled on the power play (30th). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so good looks are likely to be hard to come by for them. As for the Avalanche, they do a lot of their shooting from distance (lowest) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). Colorado has scored 4.15 goals a game, the second most in the league. The Avs are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Flames.

Joel Farabee (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, with nine points in his last five games. Matvei Gridin (5 G / 5 A / 10 P in 13 GP) has a team-high five goals, with seven points in his last five games. Nathan MacKinnon (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 13 GP) leads the Avalanche in scoring and is tied for fifth in the NHL, with a point in five straight games against Calgary. Artturi Lehkonen (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 13 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for fourth in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.

Arsenii Sergeev is expected to start for Calgary, his first start of the season, and Mackenzie Blackwood (6-3-0 / .894 SV% in 9 GS) for Colorado. Blackwood has a .939 save percentage in five starts against the Flames, well above his usual .905. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Avalanche usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.

items.text: The Flames are newly without Devin Cooley, have been without Samuel Honzek, Joel Hanley and Connor Zary for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season. Arsenii Sergeev is expected to start.
Artturi Lehkonen has ten goals on chances worth about 4.4 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
NHL.com projects Noah Juulsen back in the lineup after he was scratched for three straight games.
Zachary L'Heureux and Matt Coronato fought the last time these two met.
